messages:
Anna Li: Quick intake — new model arrived from model-curation: llamaX-13B-xt. Need a quant strategy + calibration checklist before we promote it to hosted catalog. Goal: ~2.5x cost reduction vs fp16, p95 latency <80ms on smallbatch, quality regressions <=1% on our core evals. What should be our sweep order and acceptance criteria?

Miguel Ortega: +1. I ran a quick fp8 prototype locally. Initial numbers: fp8 (e4m3) ~= 0.5% avg delta on our llama-eval set; int8 (gptq) ~= 1.9% but gives better throughput. We should pick primary (safer) and fallback (cheaper) paths.

Sasha Patel: Agree we should stage it. Proposal: fp8 primary + int8 aggressive fallback. But we need per-task sensitivity: code-gen vs summarization vs dialogue. Suggest micro-sweep with 500 examples/task (diverse prompts) to triage sensitivity before full calibration.

Leo Park: Staged calibration plan I suggest: 1) microcalib (500 samples/task) to map failure modes, 2) full calib (5k samples) for production candidates, 3) 24h shadowing / traffic shadow A/B before canary. Also run KV cache profiling and tokenization edgecases. Use existing tooling: `calib-run` + `eval-harness`. Example commands:
```
# micro calibration (fp8)
calib-run --model llamaX-13B-xt --quant fp8-e4m3 --samples 500 --out calib/fp8-micro-1925001234.jsonl

# gptq int8 sweep (per-layer)
gptq-sweep --model llamaX-13B-xt --per-layer --samples 500 --out calib/int8-sweep-1925001234.jsonl

# run eval harness
eval-harness --model ./quant/model.gguf --suites conv,summarize,code --output eval/1925001234.json
```

ci-bot: calib job queued: `calib/1925001234-fp8-micro` (500 samples). ETA ~2h.

Anna Li: Great — Miguel can you own the int8 GGTQ runs? Sasha you own fp8 configs and eval scripts. I'll update the intake doc and open the canary ticket + tagging for gguf packaging and quant metadata. Acceptance heuristic: if fp8 microcalib <=0.8% avg task delta and no critical hallucination increase -> promote to full calib.

Miguel Ortega: On it. Note: log perplexity, exact-match / BLEU / Rouge where applicable, and hallucination probes (we have the probe set in eval-probes). Also capture cost/latency per token at batch sizes [1,4,8].

Sasha Patel: I'll add a tiny PR checklist: include quant config, calibration seed, sampling script, eval suite, latency/cost table, and packaging test for gguf. Will also add a note to avoid using only token-loss as a gating metric.

Anna Li: :thumbsup: Posting results here when microcalib finishes. If fp8 microcalib passes (<=0.8% drop) we can schedule a canary next week and start traffic shadowing after canary smoke.
